findings.title: Commits lack DCO Signed-off-by trailer required by contributing.md
findings.claim: All three commits (f545c28a, 5e25ebdb, 69da8f5b) are missing a Signed-off-by trailer, violating doc/contributing.md's requirement to use git commit -s for DCO.

findings.title: Commits and PR body carry Claude attribution trailers/lines
findings.claim: All three commits carry 'Co-Authored-By: Claude ...' trailers and the PR body has a 'Generated with Claude Code' line, violating the user's global CLAUDE.md attribution rule.

findings.title: New doxygen comment stacked on old comment leaves two comment styles on one declaration
findings.claim: At rpc_types.hh:343 and :390, a new '///' doxygen block is stacked on top of the pre-existing '// send data Out...' / '// receive data In...' comment, leaving two comment styles; the old line should be folded in or dropped.

findings.title: const_cast used to mutate from const negotiate() instead of a mutable member
findings.claim: rpc_test.cc:1957 uses const_cast<hook_capturing_compressor_factory*>(this)->hooks.push_back(...); the existing cfactory in the same file solves the same problem with a mutable member instead.

findings.title: static inline const sstring name declaration differs from neighbouring patterns
findings.claim: rpc_test.cc:1940 uses 'static inline const sstring name' which differs from neighbouring patterns of a member 'name' or a function-local 'static const'; cosmetic.

findings.title: Exchange/then_wrapped/ignore_ready_future shape confirmed consistent with existing…
findings.claim: The std::exchange + then_wrapped + ignore_ready_future() shape at rpc.cc:562-570 matches stop_send_loop() (rpc.cc:225-228) and send() (rpc.cc:325); explicitly checked and found consistent, no finding.

findings.title: _stream_closing placement/comment confirmed consistent with _sink_closed_future
findings.claim: _stream_closing at rpc.hh:307 is placed and commented like _sink_closed_future above it; explicitly checked and found fine.

findings.title: Possible duplicated code between test_socket_impl and rpc_socket_impl
findings.claim: test_socket_impl::set_reuseaddr/get_reuseaddr/shutdown (1922-1935) repeat rpc_socket_impl (lines 157-175); noted as a possible duplication smell but deemed unavoidable since no reusable wrapper exists in tests/unit.

findings.title: test_connected_socket_impl is a 16-method pure forwarder (possible Middle Man)
findings.claim: test_connected_socket_impl (1900-1919) is flagged as a possible Middle Man smell, but since connected_socket_impl is abstract and no reusable wrapper exists, this is deemed unavoidable.

findings.title: No Mysterious Names, Speculative Generality or Shotgun Surgery smells found
findings.claim: Checked for Mysterious Names, Speculative Generality and Shotgun Surgery smells; flag, check, drain and test are minimal and co-located, so none found.

findings.title: send() confirmed to correctly return closed_error once _stream_closing is set
findings.claim: send() (rpc.cc:293) returns closed_error once _stream_closing is set; the expired-timeout early return is inside the guarded branch and cannot bypass it. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: _outgoing_queue_ready synchronization confirmed safe against races with stream_close()
findings.claim: _outgoing_queue_ready is the last accepted entry's done future, set only after send_entry() writes and flushes; nothing accepted before the flag can be un-chained when stream_close() exchanges it, and nothing can exchange it afterwards since send() is refused; exceptional case handled by then_wrapped/ignore_ready_future. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: write_buf.close() call sites and stream_close() reachability confirmed safe for…
findings.claim: write_buf.close() has only two call sites (rpc.cc:231, :569); stream_close() is reached only via close_sink()/close_source() (rpc.hh:346-361), so the flag is never set on a non-stream connection, and server stream connections share the same code so the server side is covered. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: PR claim that setting _error instead is not an option confirmed to hold
findings.claim: The PR's claim that 'setting _error instead is not an option' holds: abort() skips shutdown_input() if _error is set, and stop_send_loop() calls shutdown_output() immediately. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: client_factory.hooks.back() confirmed to correctly capture the stream connection's hook
findings.claim: client_factory.hooks.back() is indeed the stream connection's hook because the parent negotiates before make_stream_sink() returns, and the catch swallows only closed_error. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: Docs claim that dropping an unclosed sink is an error confirmed accurate
findings.claim: ~sink_impl asserts sink_closed() (rpc_impl.hh:935), so the doc claim 'dropping an unclosed sink is an error' is true; rpc::source has no close(). Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: 'Refs #3653' confirmed to correctly point to a related but distinct bug
findings.claim: The 'Refs #3653' reference resolves upstream to a related but distinct bug, and is appropriate. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: Server-side window fix is untested
findings.claim: server_factory.hooks is captured but never used at rpc_test.cc:1966-1970; only the client's stream stream_close() is exercised, even though the spec states the same code serves server::connection so the server side is exposed too.

findings.title: Test hangs instead of failing cleanly on an unexpected exception
findings.claim: If the hook throws anything other than closed_error, the exception propagates before st.release_close.set_value() (line 2017 vs :2026), so the parked data_sink::close() never resolves and the failure shows as a hang or ~sink_impl assert; a scope guard releasing the close would fix this.

findings.title: Doc overstates that a throw always closes the source
findings.claim: doc/rpc-streaming.md:111-112 and rpc_types.hh:387 claim throwing is what closes the source, but only failures from stream_receive() call close_source() (rpc_impl.hh:961-966); an exception thrown by unmarshall inside process_one_buffer (rpc_impl.hh:942-949) propagates without closing the source, so the claim is not strictly accurate.

findings.title: Disclosed scope expansion beyond the referenced issue
findings.claim: Commit 69da8f5b (doc section + doxygen) is a scope expansion not requested by upstream issue #3663, but the PR description declares it and marks it as non-backport.

findings.title: Claim that the test fails without the fix could not be verified (no build)
findings.claim: The claim that the test fails without the fix is plausible from output_stream::close()/flush() behavior but was not verified, since there is no build/ directory in this checkout so the test could not be run.

findings.title: Commit subject prefixes confirmed to comply with repo convention
findings.claim: Subject prefixes (rpc:, rpc_test:) comply with repository convention. Checked and confirmed correct.

findings.title: Code confirmed to comply with coding-style.md (tabs, line length, generic lambdas)
findings.claim: Checked against coding-style.md (which the sub-agent didn't see): no tabs, no C++ lines over 160 chars, no generic lambdas found; clean.
